newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Twenty eight busted in Vietnam drugs scandal.
newsitem.headline: Twenty eight busted in Vietnam drugs scandal.

text.p: Vietnam said on Thursday that 28 people, including senior police officers and a border guard, had been arrested in a widening drugs scandal rocking the communist country's security establishment.

The official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) named the policemen involved and said they had been arrested on charges including "irresponsibilities causing serious losses" and "false compilation of dossiers".
Included among the five were a lieutenant-colonel, major-colonel and deputy departmental head at the Interior Ministry, arguably Vietnam's most powerful government agency.
All were connected to the ministry's anti-drugs squad. VNA quoted Hanoi police as saying the investigation was still unfolding.
The arrests represent a significant embarrassment for Vietnam's security establishment.

They follow the death row confession of a Laotian drug trafficker who broke down in front of a firing squad earlier this year and promised to provide information on accomplices in return for a stay of execution.
The Laotian, Sieng Pheng, was arrested last year with 15.5 kilos (34 lb) of heroin concealed in his car.
It was not yet clear whether his stay of execution will be made permanent.
